Trying to replicate this, but am unable to truncate the tables in MySQL easily.
We could still try to catch the exception but I’m not sure we can just say that the problem is the table data is missing.
Keeping this open for now, but it appears to be a transient issue caused by user intervention directly on the database tables.
This seems to have involved direct access to the underlying tables, which can be dangerous. If someone else experiences this hopefully they will search Jira.

fields.summary: PUT to Fedora with inconsistent database tables causes 500 Server Error

comments.body: If my guesses above are correct (i.e. truncating the table on a running system), I don’t know that this is a solvable issue. But perhaps a try { } catch in getRdfTypeIdDirect that forces the type to be inserted at that moment.

Trying to replicate this, but am unable to truncate the tables in MySQL easily.

mysql> truncate search_resource_rdf_type;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.05 sec)

mysql> truncate table search_rdf_type;
ERROR 1701 (42000): Cannot truncate a table referenced in a foreign key constraint (`fcrepo`.`search_resource_rdf_type`, CONSTRAINT `search_resource_rdf_type_ibfk_2`)

We could still try to catch the exception but I’m not sure we can just say that the problem is the table data is missing.
Keeping this open for now, but it appears to be a transient issue caused by user intervention directly on the database tables.
This seems to have involved direct access to the underlying tables, which can be dangerous. If someone else experiences this hopefully they will search Jira.
